source.check: returned unopposed: 'Mr. Samuel Kirkpatrick, who was nominated as an independent Unionist in Clogher division having withdrawn, Mr. W. H. Boyd (U.), the sitting member, has been returned unopposed' (Ulster Herald, 29 April 1933, p. 4; also Belfast News-Letter, 26 April 1933, p. 6)

note: Triennial rural district council election. Polling in Tyrone took place on Wednesday 31 May 1933. Nominations were received by Mr. John F. M'Crea, returning officer: nine Unionists and five Nationalists were returned unopposed, and two divisions had two nominations, Clogher (W. H. Boyd, Unionist, and Samuel Kirkpatrick, Ind. Unionist) and Augher (Impartial Reporter, 20 April 1933, p. 5). Augher was the only contest polled in the Clogher district, and in Clogher division Mr. Samuel Kirkpatrick withdrew, leaving Mr. W. H. Boyd (U.), the sitting member, returned unopposed (Ulster Herald, 29 April 1933, p. 4). Labels are the paper's group headings. Filed on 1933-05-31, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Tyrone that year (confirmed). The sitting member; his Independent Unionist opponent withdrew. Returned unopposed.
